description: The Economic Survey is a flagship annual document issued by the Ministry of Finance. It provides a detailed analysis of the Indian economy's performance in the previous financial year and outlines future economic prospects.

sections.title: Basic Concepts and History
sections.description: Background of the Economic Survey, the institutions responsible for drafting it, and its historical evolution.

key_concepts.explanation: The flagship annual report of the government that reviews the state of the economy, highlights current economic trends, and suggests policy initiatives for future growth.
A department under the Ministry of Finance that is responsible for drafting the Economic Survey under the guidance and supervision of the Chief Economic Advisor (CEA).

historical_events.significance: The first Economic Survey of India was presented. Initially, it used to be presented along with the Union Budget.
The Economic Survey was decoupled from the Union Budget. Since then, it is traditionally presented one day before the presentation of the Union Budget.

sections.title: Macroeconomic Indicators
sections.description: Key economic parameters used to measure the overall health, stability, and trajectory of the economy.

key_concepts.explanation: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during a specific financial year.
The difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts (excluding borrowings). It essentially indicates the total borrowing requirements of the government.
Government funds spent on acquiring, building, or upgrading physical assets like roads, bridges, and infrastructure, which boost future economic productivity.

important_facts.fact: The survey analyzes inflation trends primarily using two major indices: the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for retail inflation and the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for wholesale inflation.
It evaluates the Current Account Deficit (CAD), which measures the gap between the value of imports and exports of goods, services, and investment incomes.

sections.title: Sector-wise Performance
sections.description: Contribution, growth trends, and analysis of the Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary sectors of the Indian economy.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the backbone of rural India, providing livelihood to the largest segment of the population and ensuring national food security.
This sector acts as an engine of growth, heavily supported by government initiatives like 'Make in India' and Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes.
It is the largest contributor to India's total Gross Value Added (GVA) and acts as the biggest magnet for Foreign Direct Investment (FDI).

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Directly asked crucial facts regarding the nature, structure, presentation, and significance of the Economic Survey.

important_facts.fact: It is neither constitutionally binding nor legally mandatory for the government to present the Economic Survey or follow its policy recommendations.
The Economic Survey is presented in both Houses of Parliament by the Finance Minister during the Budget Session.
A high level of Foreign Exchange Reserves (Forex) highlighted in the survey indicates the country's strong resilience against external economic shocks.
The survey is generally published in two volumes: Volume 1 focuses on macroeconomic challenges and policy prescriptions, while Volume 2 provides a detailed sector-wise data review of the past year.
